item.title: AI System Audit Workpaper
item.body_md:
## How to use this workpaper

One workpaper per system. Copy it, fill the header, and work the controls in order — later controls assume the earlier ones told you what the system is.

The column that matters is **evidence obtained**, not conclusion. An audit that records conclusions without the artefact behind them cannot be re-performed, and a test that cannot be re-performed did not happen.

Where a control does not apply, write why. Blank means not tested.

---

**System:** [NAME]  ·  **Owner:** [ROLE]  ·  **Period:** [FROM] to [TO]
**Auditor:** [NAME]  ·  **Fieldwork completed:** [DATE]

---

## A. Governance

**A1 — The system is authorised.**
Test: trace the system to a documented approval by whoever holds that authority.
Evidence: approval record naming the decider and the date; conditions attached.
Finding if absent: the organisation is running a system nobody approved. Rate this on consequence, not on the paperwork gap.

**A2 — Accountability is held by a person.**
Test: ask three people who owns the system. Compare answers.
Evidence: role documented; the named holder is aware they hold it.
Finding if absent: ownership by committee, which in practice means ownership by nobody at the moment it fails.

**A3 — The system appears in the AI register.**
Test: reconcile the register against systems actually running, from a source independent of the register itself — expense records, vendor invoices, SSO logs.
Evidence: reconciliation with exceptions listed.
Finding if absent: the register describes what was declared, not what is running. Report the reconciliation gap as the finding, not the missing entry.

## B. Data

**B1 — Data sources are known and lawful.**
Test: list sources; for personal data, obtain the stated lawful basis; for third-party data, obtain the licence.
Evidence: source inventory; DPIA or equivalent where required.
Finding if absent: unable to demonstrate lawful basis, which is a different and more serious finding than an unlawful basis.

**B2 — Data leaving the organisation is controlled.**
Test: determine what the vendor receives, retains and may train on. Obtain the contract clause, not the marketing page.
Evidence: contract extract; configuration screenshot showing retention settings as claimed.
Finding if absent: the control exists in the vendor FAQ and not in the agreement.

## C. Performance

**C1 — The system was tested on data it had not seen.**
Test: obtain evaluation results and confirm the test data was held out.
Evidence: dated results; description of the test set.
Finding if absent: performance is asserted rather than measured.

**C2 — Performance is measured where it matters, not only on average.**
Test: obtain results broken down by the groups the system affects.
Evidence: subgroup results, or a documented reason none are possible.
Finding if absent: aggregate performance conceals the failure that produces the complaint.

**C3 — The tested configuration is the deployed configuration.**
Test: compare model version, prompt, settings and retrieval sources between the evaluation and production.
Evidence: version identifiers from both.
Finding if absent: the evaluation describes a system that is not the one running. This is the most commonly missed control here and the one most likely to invalidate every other result.

## D. Operation

**D1 — A human can intervene, and does.**
Test: identify the override; sample occasions when it was used.
Evidence: log of overrides; interview with the person expected to exercise it.
Finding if absent: an override nobody has ever used is a control on paper. Ask what would have to happen for it to be used, and whether that person would know in time.

**D2 — Output is monitored for quality, not only availability.**
Test: obtain the monitoring definition and a sample review.
Evidence: dated review records; thresholds and who acts on them.
Finding if absent: the system can be wrong at full uptime, indefinitely, and nothing in the monitoring would say so.

**D3 — Incidents are captured and closed.**
Test: trace reported problems from user report to resolution.
Evidence: incident records with dates and outcomes.
Finding if absent: complaints are being handled individually and no pattern is visible to anyone.

---

## Rating findings

Rate on consequence and likelihood, and state both. Avoid rating on how difficult the fix is — remediation effort belongs in the management response, and mixing it into the rating is how a serious finding becomes a medium.

## Management response

Each finding needs an owner by name, an action, and a date. A response reading noted or under review is not a response, and should be recorded as declined so the acceptance of risk is visible to whoever reads this next.
item.summary: A testing programme for one AI system: eleven controls, the evidence each requires, and what a finding looks like when the evidence is missing.
item.audience: Internal auditors, and second-line reviewers testing an AI system for the first time
